Chapter 255-0252: Guo the Madman, Xie the Flirt, and the Others All Bought Houses

On the flight back to Beijing, Chen Guiliang sat in economy class, just like his employees.

His bodyguard, Yang Shuo, was seated next to him.

Chen Guiliang closed his eyes to doze, vaguely hearing Xu Fengyin's voice from the row behind: "Is this your first time on a plane?"

"Yes," said Ding Beili. "I've never left Shanghai before."

She came from an ordinary Shanghai family. Life wasn't too bad, but it was far from wealthy.

When she said she was going to Beijing for work, her parents nearly had a fight over it. Her father was against it, her mother was for it, and they argued endlessly.

Ding Beili pulled her parents in front of the computer, opened Xiaonei, Hainei, Youke Platform, and the official Legends of the Three Kingdoms website, pointing to them and saying her boss had made all of them. Then she searched Baidu for web pages related to Chen Guiliang and let her parents slowly read the news.

What finally made her father agree was not Chen Guiliang's net worth of billions, but a special interview article from China Youth Daily that was reposted by NetEase.

That report was very comprehensive, covering Chen Guiliang's life from childhood all the way to his time at Peking University.

It was incredibly inspirational!

Game Science hadn't even really started operating, and Ding Beili was already famous.

A few dirty old men who had specifically come to photograph Xu Fengyin ended up snapping pictures of Ding Beili as well, killing two birds with one stone.

They also discovered that Ding Beili didn't smile the entire time, making her the only showgirl at the entire ChinaJoy expo who never smiled.

Even Ding Beili's Xiaonei account was dug up. Her last three journal entries were:

"Still can't find a full-time job, but I signed up for a part-time gig on Xiaonei and was chosen by Game Science. Does anyone know how to be a showgirl? I've only ever handed out flyers before."

"Today the boss said I have a good image and asked if I wanted to go work in Beijing. I've never traveled far from home before, so I'm a little excited and a little scared."

"I'm flying on a plane tomorrow, I've never been on a plane before."

These three journal entries received a large number of comments.

Those who could access Xiaonei were, of course, current students or graduates who had previously registered on the site.

Unfortunately, on Xiaonei, you could only add friends, not follow strangers.

"Hey girl, you should hurry and register a Hainei account. I'll definitely follow you!"

"Damn, Chen Guiliang just takes any beauty he sees. Is he planning to build a golden house to hide his mistress?"

"Definitely. He recruits beautiful women into his company so he can be the first to get to them."

"So she was really selected from an online application? Youke has always had a good eye for beauties. Last year's Xu Fengyin was even prettier."

"Xu Fengyin was already a graphic artist at Youke. Do you understand the value of the lead artist for *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*?"

"Haha, too bad Old Xu's dark past was dug up. She didn't reply to netizens for a long time."

"Hey, this is Ding Beili's account, can you not discuss other girls here?"

"Everyone, go look at Xu Fengyin's Hainei photo album! One of the photos is a group picture of Old Xu and Ding Beili. A dream collaboration!"

For some inexplicable reason, a new crowd of people flocked to Xu Fengyin's Hainei account to spectate.

Beautiful women really did attract attention and could bring publicity to a game.

Last year, when Xu Fengyin's cosplay photos as Zhen Ji went viral, a whole wave of passersby asked what character it was. After learning the Zhen Ji design was from *Legends of the Three Kingdoms*, many netizens went to play the game because of it.

It happened again this year, and even more directly.

Because the small tube top Ding Beili wore had a very distinct Legends of the Three Kingdoms logo printed on its chest.

The plane took off.

Xu Fengyin said, "It's hard to rent a place near the company right now. You can look online. I'll also help ask around in my residential complex."

"Thank you, Fengyin-jie." Ding Beili felt a little more at ease. For a girl all alone, having an big sister figure to help was for the best.

When Chen Guiliang had just started his business, the company only had a few employees, so they could temporarily stay in Changchun Xinyuan. But they couldn't live there as of last year. Even those who had already moved in had to move out and find their own places.

The second batch of employees mostly rented in Yandongyuan.

Yandongyuan was a faculty dormitory area. Its property rights belonged to Peking University, and it was strictly forbidden to rent to non-university personnel. The faculty would sublet illegally in private, and since it was to employees from the Peking University Science Park, the university authorities usually turned a blind eye.

The problem was, someone reported it!

A few family members of the faculty were very unhappy about non-university personnel appearing in their complex. After multiple consecutive reports, Peking University had no choice but to send people to clear them out, giving all the tenants a deadline to move out.

Now, many employees from the companies in the PKU Science and Technology Building had moved to the old, small, and shabby apartments in the Zhongguan West District.

That was the family residential area for institutions like the Chinese Academy of Sciences, Peking University, and Tsinghua University. The oldest buildings were already half a century old, about the same age as New China...

The apartment Xie Yang was currently renting belonged to a former Tsinghua professor, and the professor's parents lived next door. That old couple were also retired Tsinghua professors and often chatted with Xie Yang.

The executives at Bytedance and Youke were all now thinking about buying property.

Xie Yang had his eye on a residential development not far from the company, so the prices were also expensive. The average price was 20,000 yuan per square meter. For a 100-square-meter apartment, the down payment would be around 500,000 yuan.

Xie Yang's current annual salary was 280,000 yuan—it had been raised after the Series B financing; he earned less last year. But including the year-end bonus, he could make a little over 400,000 yuan.

He had saved money for a year and a half, just enough for the down payment.

When Guo Feng, Ao Yanchen, Dong Qianqiu, and the others heard that Xie Yang was looking at properties, they also got the idea to buy.

Sigh, they were all recent graduates, yet they could already buy homes and settle down near Zhongguancun.

If word of this got out, people would be green with envy.

In the last two years, as university students from the expanded enrollment began to graduate, the salaries of graduates from less prestigious universities were actually declining.

The monthly salary for graduates from the worst universities, working in less developed cities, had even dropped below 1,000 yuan. This had even sparked heated discussions in the media, saying that not all university students were the chosen ones anymore.

The plane landed at Capital Airport, and the company's big Jinbei van had been waiting for a long time.

Xu Fengyin was definitely a looks-supremacist. The amount she spoke depended on the attractiveness of her conversation partner, regardless of gender.

Facing Ding Beili, Xu Fengyin became much more talkative, chattering away and introducing the Beijing streetscapes all the way.

Back at the Game Science company, Dong Qianqiu came to find Chen Guiliang. "Boss, a few of us have bought houses. We went together to sign the contracts yesterday."

"Where at?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Dong Qianqiu said, "Huaqing Jiayuan."

"I knew it," Chen Guiliang remarked.

The land for that shabby residential complex had been acquired back in 1994. Later, the built houses couldn't sell, so they were sold off to China Resources Land. The floor price was 4,000 yuan per square meter, and China Resources was mocked for being a fool taking over the mess.

In 2000, when the third phase opened, it was renamed "Huaqing Jiayuan," with a pre-sale price of 5,000 yuan per square meter. It was cursed by the common people for being too expensive.

In 2001, it rose to 7,000.

In 2005, it rose to 10,000.

And now it was even more ridiculous, doubling directly to 20,000!

Why was it rising so fiercely?

Because the era of insane internet venture capital had arrived.

The housing prices of Huaqing Jiayuan were driven up by internet company executives like Dong Qianqiu, Guo Feng, Ao Yanchen, and Xie Yang. Many of the homeowners in the third phase were major figures in the internet industry.

The complex was west of Zhongguancun, east of Wudaokou, and north of Tsinghua University. Children could attend Zhongguan Erxiao.

"A few of us discussed it. When we move in, we'll all have a meal together," Dong Qianqiu said.

Chen Guiliang said, "Alright. I'll come congratulate you on your housewarming then."

Dong Qianqiu said, "Boss, you should buy a place too. If we all live in the same building, it'll be convenient to meet up and communicate in the future."

Chen Guiliang said, "I'll go take a look some other day."

The housing prices in that shabby complex would double again to 40,000 in another two or three years.

After handling some documents at Youke, Chen Guiliang went upstairs to Bytedance, where those three guys also came over to talk about buying houses.

"You guys! The Xiongnu have not yet been vanquished, how can you think of starting a family! The company is still in its growth phase, and you're already thinking about enjoying life," Chen Guiliang scolded them for a bit, then complained, "Damn it, you all buy houses as a group and don't even call me. You signed the contracts while I was away."
